sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design Ola at the scale of ~1.5 M daily rides across 250+ Indian cities: ride-hailing with **driver-rider matching** (dispatch), **surge pricing**, **geospatial indexing** (H3 + Redis GEO), **multi-city** sharding, **payment** (UPI / Ola Money wallet / cash), and **safety features** (live ride tracking, SOS button, OTP-verified pickup, audio recording). Focus on the **dispatch algorithm** (find nearest driver in < 3 s), **surge pricing** (dynamic multiplier per H3 hexagon), and **Indian-market considerations** (low-bandwidth networks, multi-language, UPI dominance, regulatory compliance per state, female-rider safety). ---

### Functional Requirements
- **Request a ride**: rider enters pickup + destination; app shows fare estimate + ETA + surge; rider confirms.
- **Ride types**: Micro (hatchback), Mini (sedan), Prime Sedan, Prime SUV, Auto, Bike, E-rickshaw, Kaali Peeli (Mumbai taxi), Outstation (intercity), Rental (hourly).
- **Driver matching (dispatch)**: find nearest available driver within ~3 s; auto-assign (Ola's model — driver has 15 s to acknowledge, not accept/reject).
- **Real-time tracking**: rider sees driver location; driver sees rider location; updated every 3 s.
- **Trip lifecycle**: `requested → matched → en_route → pickup → in_progress → drop_off → completed` (plus `cancelled`, `no_show`).
- **Surge pricing**: dynamic multiplier (1.0×–2.5×) per H3 hexagon based on supply/demand.
- **Fare calculation**: base fare + distance (per km) + time (per min) + surge + booking fee + tolls + GST; auto-detects toll zones.
- **Payments**: UPI (60% of rides), Ola Money wallet, credit/debit card, cash (10–15% of rides, mostly tier-2/3).
- **Safety features**: OTP-verified pickup (rider tells driver the OTP), live ride sharing (send trip link to family), SOS button (alerts police + Ola safety team + trusted contacts), in-app audio recording (optional, on rider opt-in), female-rider "Women" mode (assigns only female drivers).
- **Ratings**: rider rates driver, driver rates rider (1–5 stars); below 4.5 = warnings.
- **Driver onboarding**: signup, document verification (Aadhaar, driving licence, RC, insurance), background check, vehicle inspection.
- **Push notifications**: ride status updates, surge alerts, promotions, earnings dashboards for drivers.
- **Multi-language**: app + SMS in Hindi, English, and 8+ regional languages (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Malayalam).
- **Driver app**: go-online, navigate, mark arrived/start/end trip, earnings dashboard, incentive tracker.

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.95% for dispatch (≈ 4.4 h downtime/year) — a missed ride = lost revenue + driver churn.
- **Latency**: driver match p99 < 3 s; driver location update p99 < 500 ms; fare estimate p99 < 1 s; surge lookup p99 < 50 ms.
- **Scale**: 1.5 M rides/day, ~50 M MAU, ~2.5 M active drivers, 250+ cities.
- **Throughput**: ~3 M driver location updates per minute at peak (each driver pings every 3 s); ~100 ride requests/s globally.
- **Storage**: 1.5 M rides/day × 10 KB metadata + 3 MB GPS track = ~4.5 TB/day; 3-year retention.
- **Geospatial**: "find nearest N drivers within radius R" in < 100 ms across 2.5 M drivers.
- **Consistency**: strong for ride state machine (a driver can't be matched to two riders); eventual for location (3 s lag OK).
- **Multi-region**: India-only (data residency); active-active across Mumbai + Hyderabad DCs.
- **Low-bandwidth tolerance**: rider app must work on 2G/3G (compress payloads, fallback to SMS notifications); driver app must work offline-first (queue location updates locally).

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- **Location updates**: 2.5 M drivers × 1 ping/3 s = ~830 K pings/s globally. Each ping = 100 bytes = ~83 MB/s ingress.
- **Dispatch QPS**: 1.5 M rides/day ÷ 86 400 s = ~17 rides/s avg, peak commute (5× avg) = ~85/s.
- **Geospatial index**: 2.5 M drivers in Redis GEO. Per-city sharding: top 10 cities hold 60% of drivers. A typical city dispatch query scans ~500 candidates in < 50 ms.
- **Ride storage**: 1.5 M rides/day × 3 MB GPS = 4.5 TB/day → ~1.6 PB/year. Hot 30 days → SSD; older → S3/Glacier.
- **Surge**: recomputed every minute per H3 hexagon (~200 K hexagons across India's urban areas = ~3.3 K surge updates/s).
- **UPI transactions**: ~900 K UPI rides/day × 1 UPI debit = ~900 K UPI transactions/day = ~10/s avg, ~50/s peak.

### Scope
- **In scope**: ride request, dispatch (driver matching), surge pricing, real-time tracking, ride lifecycle, geospatial indexing, scaling, multi-region, safety features, UPI/wallet payments.
- **Out of scope**: Ola Foods (food delivery, similar to Swiggy), Ola Electric (EVs — separate app), Ola Store (grocery), self-driving R&D, full maps/routing (use Ola Maps — in-house OSM-based, or Mapbox/Google Maps as fallback), full ML for ETA (black box), regulatory compliance per state (mention but don't deep-dive).

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **DNS + CDN** (Route 53 + CloudFront/Akamai) — routes app to nearest regional API, serves static assets. 2. **API Gateway** (Kong/Envoy) — TLS, OAuth/JWT, rate limiting, request routing, mobile BFF, multi-language payload negotiation. 3. **Microservices**: - **Rider service**: profile, payment methods, ride history, saved places (Home, Work). - **Driver service**: profile, vehicle, document verification, status (online/offline/busy), incentive tracking. - **Ride service**: the state machine (`requested → matched → en_route → pickup → in_progress → drop_off → completed`). - **Dispatch service**: the core matching algorithm — finds nearest driver within seconds; auto-assignment. - **Surge service**: computes dynamic pricing per H3 hexagon, every minute. - **ETA service**: predicts travel time using ML (XGBoost on historical traffic + road network graph). - **Pricing service**: calculates fare (base + distance + time + surge + booking fee + tolls + GST). - **Geolocation service**: stores driver locations, supports "nearest N within radius" queries. Redis GEO (geohash-backed sorted set) + H3 cell routing. - **Map matching service**: snaps noisy GPS pings to the road network graph (Hidden Markov Model); Ola Maps in-house. - **Payment service**: UPI (via Razorpay/Pine Labs/Cashfree), Ola Money wallet, cards, cash ledger. - **Notification service**: FCM/APNS push, SMS (MSG91), WhatsApp business, IVR for OTP. - **Rating service**: post-ride ratings. - **Safety service**: SOS handler, live ride sharing, audio recording storage, trusted-contact notifications. - **Women-mode service**: filters drivers by gender for female riders opting in. 4. **Geospatial index** — Redis GEO (sorted set on geohash) for driver locations; H3 hexagons (level 8, ~0.7 km²) for surge cells and city sharding. 5. **Kafka** — event backbone. Topics: `ride-events`, `driver-location`, `surge-updates`, `payment-events`, `safety-events`. Consumers: dispatch, surge, analytics, fraud, safety. 6. **Cassandra** — ride history, GPS tracks, driver/rider profiles. Multi-region replicated. 7. **MySQL/Aurora** — transactional data (payments, wallet balances, driver payouts, vehicle docs). 8. **Redis** — geospatial index, ride state cache, surge cache, driver status, session state. 9. **Schema Registry** (Confluent) — Avro schemas for Kafka events. 10. **ClickHouse/Pinot** — real-time analytics (driver supply, ride volume, surge effectiveness, city dashboards). 11. **Ola Maps / Mapbox / Google Maps** — map tiles, routing, ETA baseline. Ola Maps is in-house OSM-based. 12. **WebSocket gateway** — for real-time driver location streaming to rider app (and vice versa). 13. **UPI gateway** — integrates with Razorpay/Juspay/Pine Labs for UPI collect; NPCI Bhim for direct UPI. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR R([Rider App]) --> DNS[Route 53 + CDN] D([Driver App]) --> DNS DNS --> GW[API Gateway + WS] GW --> RSVC[Rider svc] GW --> DSVC[Driver svc] GW --> RIDE[Ride svc] GW --> DISP[Dispatch svc] GW --> LOC[Geolocation svc] GW --> WS[WebSocket gateway] GW --> SAFE[Safety svc] WS --> R WS --> D D -->|ping every 3s| LOC LOC --> GEO[(Redis GEO
driver index)] LOC --> K2[(Kafka: driver-location)] R -->|request ride| RIDE RIDE --> DISP DISP --> GEO DISP --> SURGE[Surge svc] DISP --> ETA[ETA svc] DISP --> DSVC DSVC -->|assign + 15s ack| D D -->|ack| DSVC DSVC --> RIDE RIDE --> K1[(Kafka: ride-events)] K1 --> PAY[Payment svc] K1 --> NOTIF[Notification svc] K1 --> AN[(ClickHouse analytics)] K1 --> SAFE K2 --> MM[Map matching] K2 --> SURGE SURGE --> SC[(Redis surge cache)] SURGE --> K3[(Kafka: surge-updates)] PAY --> UPI[(UPI gateway
Razorpay)] PAY --> WAL[(Ola Money wallet)] PAY --> DB[(MySQL payments)] RIDE --> CASS[(Cassandra rides + GPS)] SAFE --> S3[(S3 audio + SOS logs)] ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +-------------------+ +-------------------+ | Rider App | | Driver App | | (request ride) | | (ping every 3s) | +---+-----------+---+ +---+-----------+---+ | | | | API | | WebSocket | ping | ack v v v | +-----+-----------+----------------+-----------+----+ | API Gateway / WebSocket (per region) | +--+--+--+--+--+--+---+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+--+ | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | v v v v v v v v v v v v v v v v +------+--+ ++ +-+ ++ + +++ +--+-+ +--+-+ +--+-+ +--+---+ |Rider| |Ride| |Dispatch| |Surge| |ETA| |Pay| |Safety| |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc| |svc| |svc | +-----+ +--+-+ +---+----+ +-----+ +--+-+ +--+-+ +------+ | | | | v v v v +----+--+ +--+-------+ +--+--+ ++-----+ |Geo svc| |Redis GEO | |UPI GW| |Ola M| +-------+ |driver idx| +------+ +-----+ +----------+ ^ | (driver pings every 3s) Ride state machine: requested -> matched -> en_route -> pickup -> in_progress -> drop_off -> completed Safety flows: - OTP at pickup (rider tells driver the OTP shown in app) - SOS button -> alerts police + Ola safety + trusted contacts - Live ride sharing -> trip link with real-time GPS - Audio recording (opt-in) -> S3, deleted after 7 days ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. **Driver comes online**: Driver app `POST /api/v1/driver/online` → driver service updates status, geolocation service adds driver to Redis GEO `riders:online:{city}`. From now on, driver app sends a `location_update` event every 3 s with (lat, lon, heading, speed, status). The app also queues pings locally if offline (cap 60). 2. **Rider requests a ride**: Rider app `POST /api/v1/rides {pickup, destination, ride_type}` → ride service creates a ride in `requested` state, calls dispatch. Ride service publishes `ride-requested` event to Kafka. 3. **Dispatch (the core algorithm)**: Dispatch service calls geolocation service → finds nearest N (say 5) available drivers within radius R (say 3 km) using Redis GEO `GEORADIUS`. For each candidate, fetches ETA from ETA service. Scores by (ETA, on-time %, idle time, ride_type match). Picks the best. Sends assignment via WebSocket. Driver has 15 s to acknowledge (not accept/reject — auto-assignment). 4. **OTP at pickup**: When driver arrives, rider tells driver the 4-digit OTP shown in their app. Driver enters it → ride state `pickup → in_progress`. This prevents wrong-rider pickup (common at airports/malls). 5. **Trip in progress**: GPS track recorded (every 3 s) to Cassandra. WebSocket streams driver location to rider every 3 s. Safety service monitors for route deviation, unscheduled stops. 6. **Drop-off**: Driver marks `drop_off` → `completed`. Payment service charges rider (UPI collect, Ola Money debit, card, or cash ledger). Rating prompt sent. 7. **Surge**: Continuously (every minute per H3 hexagon), surge service consumes `ride-requested` and `driver-online` events from Kafka, computes supply/demand ratio, updates `surge:{h3}` in Redis. Pricing service uses this multiplier for fare estimates.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

**Cassandra — `rides` (ride metadata)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE rides (
    ride_id         UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    rider_id        UUID,
    driver_id       UUID,
    ride_type       TEXT,             -- micro|mini|prime_sedan|prime_suv|auto|bike|outstation|rental
    pickup_lat      DOUBLE,
    pickup_lon      DOUBLE,
    dest_lat        DOUBLE,
    dest_lon        DOUBLE,
    status          TEXT,             -- requested|matched|en_route|pickup|in_progress|drop_off|completed|cancelled
    surge_mult      DOUBLE,
    fare            DECIMAL,
    distance_m      INT,
    duration_s      INT,
    payment_method  TEXT,             -- upi|wallet|card|cash
    pickup_otp      TEXT,             -- 4-digit OTP for pickup verification
    is_women_mode   BOOLEAN,
    city_id         INT,
    requested_at    TIMESTAMP,
    completed_at    TIMESTAMP
);
```

**Cassandra — `ride_locations` (GPS trace, time-series)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE ride_locations (
    ride_id     UUID,
    ts          TIMESTAMP,
    lat         DOUBLE,
    lon         DOUBLE,
    heading     DOUBLE,
    speed       DOUBLE,
    PRIMARY KEY (ride_id, ts)
) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (ts ASC);
```

**Cassandra — `rides_by_rider`** (denormalised for rider history)
```sql
CREATE TABLE rides_by_rider (
    rider_id     UUID,
    requested_at TIMESTAMP,
    ride_id      UUID,
    status       TEXT,
    fare         DECIMAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (rider_id, requested_at)
) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (requested_at DESC);
```

**MySQL — `drivers`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE drivers (
    driver_id         BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    name              VARCHAR(200),
    phone             VARCHAR(15) UNIQUE,
    gender            CHAR(1),            -- M/F/O (used for Women-mode filtering)
    city_id           INT,
    vehicle_id        BIGINT,
    ride_types        JSON,               -- ["micro","mini"]
    rating            DECIMAL(3,2),
    rating_count      INT,
    is_verified       BOOLEAN,            -- docs + background check
    is_active         BOOLEAN,
    created_at        TIMESTAMP,
    INDEX idx_city_active (city_id, is_active),
    INDEX idx_gender (gender)
);
```

**MySQL — `wallet_balances`** (Ola Money)
```sql
CREATE TABLE wallet_balances (
    user_id      BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    balance      DECIMAL(10,2),
    currency     CHAR(3) DEFAULT 'INR',
    updated_at   TIMESTAMP,
    version      INT                 -- optimistic locking
);
```

**MySQL — `wallet_transactions`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE wallet_transactions (
    txn_id        BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id       BIGINT,
    ride_id       UUID,
    amount        DECIMAL(10,2),     -- negative for debit
    type          TEXT,              -- debit|credit|refund|topup
    reference     VARCHAR(100),      -- UPI ref / ride_id
    created_at    TIMESTAMP,
    INDEX idx_user (user_id, created_at)
);
```

**Redis GEO — `riders:online:{city}:{ride_type}`**
```
GEOADD riders:online:mumbai:micro 72.8777 19.0760 "driver_1234"
GEORADIUS riders:online:mumbai:micro 72.8777 19.0760 3 km COUNT 5 ASC WITHCOORD WITHDIST
```

**Redis — surge cache**
```
SET surge:{h3_id} 1.8 EX 300      # multiplier, 5 min TTL
```

### Indexes
- Cassandra: PK on `ride_id`; denormalised `rides_by_rider` for rider-history queries; `rides_by_driver` similarly.
- MySQL `drivers`: (city_id, is_active), (gender) for Women-mode filtering.
- MySQL `wallet_transactions`: (user_id, created_at) for statement queries.
- Redis GEO: sorted set on geohash; O(log N + M) radius scan.
- Elasticsearch (optional): not used for dispatch; only for rider-app "explore" features.

### Storage Choice
- **Cassandra** for rides & GPS traces: high write throughput (830 K pings/s), multi-region replication, time-series access pattern.
- **MySQL** for drivers, wallet, payments: ACID for wallet balance (critical — double-debit is a P0), rich secondary indexes.
- **Redis** for live driver positions, ride state cache, surge cache, OTP, session.
- **S3** for audio recordings (encrypted, 7-day TTL), SOS logs, trip screenshots.
- **ClickHouse** for analytics (columnar, fast aggregations over billions of ride rows).

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Query Redis GEO for online drivers of the right type near pickup.
- Lower = better.
- Core dispatch: auto-assign best driver; on no-ack, try next.
- Atomically debit Ola Money wallet.
- Women-mode filter: only female drivers
- Escalate: widen radius or broadcast
- Version conflict -> retry

**Defines:** `haversine_km()`, `find_candidate_drivers()`, `score_driver()`, `dispatch()`, `debit_wallet()`

### API Design
```
POST /api/v1/rides                            {pickup, destination, ride_type, is_women_mode}
GET  /api/v1/rides/{id}
POST /api/v1/rides/{id}/cancel                {reason}
POST /api/v1/rides/{id}/pickup_otp            {otp}    (driver enters)
POST /api/v1/rides/{id}/start
POST /api/v1/rides/{id}/end
POST /api/v1/rides/{id}/rate                  {rating, feedback}
GET  /api/v1/rides/{id}/track                 (or via WebSocket)
WS   /ws/v1/track/{ride_id}                   driver location stream
POST /api/v1/driver/online
POST /api/v1/driver/location                  {lat, lon, heading, speed}
POST /api/v1/driver/assignment/{id}/ack
POST /api/v1/driver/assignment/{id}/unassign  {reason}
POST /api/v1/safety/sos                       {ride_id, location}
POST /api/v1/safety/share_ride                {ride_id, contact_phone}
GET  /api/v1/wallet/balance
POST /api/v1/wallet/topup                     {amount, payment_method}
POST /api/v1/wallet/debit                     {ride_id, amount}
```

### Key Algorithms

**Dispatch — auto-assignment with ETA + Women-mode filter**
```python
import heapq, math

def haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    R = 6371.0
    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)
    dphi = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)
    dlmb = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)
    a = math.sin(dphi/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dlmb/2)**2
    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

def find_candidate_drivers(redis_geo, city, ride_type, pickup_lat, pickup_lon,
                           radius_km=3.0, limit=10):
    """Query Redis GEO for online drivers of the right type near pickup."""
    raw = redis_geo.georadius(
        f"riders:online:{city}:{ride_type}",
        pickup_lon, pickup_lat, radius_km,
        unit="km", withcoord=True, withdist=True, count=limit, sort="ASC")
    return [{
        "driver_id": r[0].decode(),
        "dist_km":   r[1],
        "lat":       r[2][1],
        "lon":       r[2][0],
    } for r in raw]

def score_driver(driver, pickup_lat, pickup_lon, eta_lookup, driver_stats):
    """Lower = better. Blends ETA, on-time %, idle time."""
    eta_min = eta_lookup(driver["driver_id"], driver["lat"], driver["lon"],
                         pickup_lat, pickup_lon)        # via Ola Maps / ETA svc
    on_time = driver_stats.get(driver["driver_id"], {}).get("on_time_pct", 0.9)
    idle_min = driver_stats.get(driver["driver_id"], {}).get("idle_min", 5)
    return (eta_min * 0.7
            + (1 - on_time) * 20.0
            + max(0, 10 - idle_min) * 0.1)

def dispatch(redis_geo, city, ride_type, pickup_lat, pickup_lon,
             eta_lookup, driver_stats, driver_meta, assigner,
             is_women_mode=False, ack_timeout_s=15, max_attempts=3):
    """Core dispatch: auto-assign best driver; on no-ack, try next."""
    candidates = find_candidate_drivers(redis_geo, city, ride_type,
                                        pickup_lat, pickup_lon)
    if not candidates:
        return None
    # Women-mode filter: only female drivers
    if is_women_mode:
        candidates = [c for c in candidates
                      if driver_meta.get(c["driver_id"], {}).get("gender") == "F"]
    if not candidates:
        return None
    scored = [(score_driver(c, pickup_lat, pickup_lon, eta_lookup, driver_stats),
               c) for c in candidates]
    heapq.heapify(scored)
    for _ in range(max_attempts):
        if not scored:
            return None
        _, driver = heapq.heappop(scored)
        ok = assigner.assign(driver["driver_id"], ride_type,
                             ack_timeout_s=ack_timeout_s)   # WS push, 15s ack
        if ok:
            return driver
    # escalate: widen radius or broadcast
    return None
```

**Wallet debit with optimistic locking (prevents double-debit)**
```python
def debit_wallet(mysql_conn, user_id, ride_id, amount):
    """Atomically debit Ola Money wallet. Uses optimistic locking."""
    for attempt in range(3):                       # retry on version conflict
        with mysql_conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT balance, version FROM wallet_balances "
                        "WHERE user_id = %s FOR UPDATE", (user_id,))
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row or row[0] < amount:
                raise InsufficientBalance()
            balance, version = row
            cur.execute(
                "UPDATE wallet_balances SET balance = balance - %s, "
                "version = version + 1, updated_at = NOW() "
                "WHERE user_id = %s AND version = %s",
                (amount, user_id, version))
            if cur.rowcount == 1:
                cur.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO wallet_transactions "
                    "(txn_id, user_id, ride_id, amount, type, reference) "
                    "VALUES (?,?,?,?, 'debit', ?)",
                    (next_id(), user_id, ride_id, -amount, str(ride_id)))
                mysql_conn.commit()
                return True
        # version conflict -> retry
    raise ConcurrentModification()
```

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **Commute peak (8–10 AM, 5–8 PM)**: 5× normal QPS. Autoscale stateless services (HPA on CPU + QPS). Pre-warm surge cache, popular-route ETAs. Over-provision dispatch workers (HPA on Kafka lag for `ride-events`).
- **Geospatial index hot spots**: a single Redis GEO key for all of Mumbai gets hammered. Shard by H3 hexagon (level 8) — `riders:online:{city}:{ride_type}:{h3}`. Cross-cell dispatch scans neighbouring H3 cells.
- **Driver location write fan-in**: 830 K pings/s. Use Redis Cluster (32 shards) + pipelined writes. Kafka spout for durability; ingestion consumer batches writes (every 100 ms).
- **Wallet consistency**: Ola Money debits must be ACID. MySQL with row-level locking + optimistic versioning. Read replicas for statement queries; writes always to master.
- **UPI payment failures**: ~5–10% UPI collect requests fail (NPCI downtime, bank issues). Retry with backoff (3 attempts, 5 s apart); fall back to Ola Money wallet if rider has balance; cash as last resort.
- **Multi-region active-active**: rides placed in Mumbai DC stay in Mumbai; Hyderabad DC serves southern cities. Cassandra `NetworkTopologyStrategy` RF=3 per DC. Cross-region only for driver/rider master data via Kafka MirrorMaker2.
- **Low-bandwidth tolerance**: rider app payloads compressed (Protobuf over JSON); SMS fallback for OTP and ride status; driver app offline-first (queues pings, retry on reconnect).
- **Women-mode supply**: female drivers are ~5–10% of fleet. Women-mode rides may have longer wait times; the app shows "Women mode: longer ETA" upfront. If no female driver within 5 km in 3 attempts, fall back to regular dispatch with rider consent.

### Caching Strategy
- **Driver live position**: Redis GEO (in-memory, hot). Sharded by H3 cell.
- **Surge**: Redis `surge:{h3_id}` TTL 5 min, refreshed by surge consumer.
- **Ride state**: Redis `ride:{id}:status` TTL 1 h, invalidated on transition.
- **ETA**: Redis `eta:{pickup_h3}:{dest_h3}:{ride_type}` TTL 60 s (for popular routes).
- **Driver profile/rating**: Redis `driver:{id}:meta` TTL 5 min.
- **OTP**: Redis `ride:{id}:pickup_otp` TTL 10 min (auto-expire after pickup window).

### Failure Modes
- **Driver doesn't ack in 15 s**: dispatch moves to next-best candidate. If 3 attempts fail, widen radius (3 km → 5 km), then broadcast with a bonus.
- **No driver available (supply crisis)**: surge spikes (cap 2.5×); rides with ETA > 12 min show "high demand" warning; very long waits (5 min) auto-cancel + no charge.
- **Driver cancels mid-ride**: rare; rider app prompts "Driver cancelled, rebooking for free" → re-dispatch with priority. Driver's cancellation rate penalised.
- **Redis GEO down**: fallback to Elasticsearch `geo_distance` query (slower but durable) or to a precomputed driver bucket in Cassandra; degraded mode flag.
- **Cassandra quorum failure**: ride writes circuit-break to 503; active-active failover to other DC; client retries with backoff.
- **UPI gateway timeout**: payment service retries 3×; if still failing, fall back to Ola Money wallet (if balance) or mark as "pay by cash" with driver confirmation.
- **Wallet double-debit risk**: optimistic locking (version column) + idempotency key on `ride_id` (UNIQUE constraint on `(ride_id, type)`). Reconciliation job nightly.
- **Kafka broker loss**: RF=3 covers; producers retry on `LEADER_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
- **Ola Maps outage**: ETA service falls back to haversine distance ÷ avg city speed; routing returns polyline from cached historical route.
- **Safety SOS**: routed to a separate high-priority queue (dedicated Redis instance + on-call safety team); never fails due to main-system load.

quiz.explanation: Three key differences rooted in the Indian market. (1) Auto-assignment vs. driver-pickup: Uber asks one driver at a time and waits for explicit accept/reject; Ola uses auto-assignment — the system picks the best driver and assigns; the driver has 15 s to acknowledge, not accept/reject. This is faster and avoids races during India's commute peaks.

Multiplier M = clamp(1.0 + 0.4 * log2(demand/supply), 1.0, 2.5) if demand > supply, else 1.0. To prevent thrash, the per-minute delta is capped at ±0.2× and hysteresis requires a 0.1× change to publish.
